translations.text: Ita: Christ came to her in the form of an infant, and it was then that she said:
Little Jesus is nursed by me in my little hermitage; though a cleric may have a great store of wealth, it is all a lie except little Jesus.
The fosterling I nurse in my house is not the fosterling of a base churl: it is Jesus, with the men of heaven, against my heart every single night.
Young little Jesus is my everlasting good: he gives, and he is not remiss [?]. Whoever does not pray to the King who has power over all things will regret it.
Noble, angelic Jesus, no slothful [?] cleric, is nursed by me in my little hermitage: Jesus, son of the Hebrew woman.
Sons of princes, sons of kings, though they come into my land, it is not from them that I expect any benefit: dearer to me is little Jesus.
Sing a fitting chorus, maidens, to the one who is entitled to your little tribute: he is in his place on high, though little Jesus is at my breast.
